players.product: high-speed DRAM / NAND memory wafer testers

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report: consolidated Q2 2026 revenue of KRW 104,991,544,809 against KRW 80,403,850,103 in Q2 2025, with operating profit of KRW 15,052,094,723 versus KRW 4,364,462,440; H1 2026 revenue of KRW 138,303,995,223 against KRW 119,364,898,147 and H1 operating profit of KRW 19,046,472,111 versus KRW 2,859,049,356. The semiconductor and electronics segment earned H1 revenue of KRW 135,104,902 thousand and operating profit of KRW 17,358,549 thousand; within it, listed subsidiary SEMCNS (37.11% owned, ceramic substrates for probe cards) had H1 revenue of KRW 58,440,046 thousand and operating profit of KRW 17,208,491 thousand, while the parent (testers) posted H1 revenue of KRW 73,231,531,791 and operating profit of KRW 228,375,175

Order book at 30 June 2026: disclosed orders of KRW 243,660 million, of which KRW 29,450 million had been delivered, leaving a backlog of KRW 214,210 million — memory tester orders of KRW 38,750 million (2025-12-18, due 2026-09-30), KRW 40,300 million (2026-03-03, due 2026-09-30) and KRW 93,000 million (2026-05-29, due 2026-11-30) plus an LPE-B upgrade order of KRW 42,160 million (2026-04-10, due 2026-12-31)
quarterly_data.figure: order backlog KRW 214,210 million (orders KRW 243,660 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Customer concentration (undisclosed names): Customer A generated KRW 66,837,185 thousand in H1 2026 (48.30% of revenue, KRW 64,914,640 thousand of it in Q2), Customer B KRW 17,613,622 thousand (12.70%) and Customer C KRW 15,106,165 thousand (10.90%), against 63.90% and 10.30% for A and B a year earlier. Export revenue was KRW 27,639 million in H1 against KRW 37,530 million for all of FY2025
quarterly_data.figure: Customer A 48.30% (KRW 66,837,185 thousand), B 12.70%, C 10.90% of H1 2026 revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and build-up: memory wafer tester capacity of 60 units in H1 2026 (120 in FY2025) against production of 32 units, a 53% utilisation (FY2025 production 55 units); raw-material inventory rose to KRW 71,340,885 thousand from KRW 40,558,481 thousand at end-2025 and work in process to KRW 44,269,153 thousand, and the group had KRW 26,619,535 thousand of committed property, plant and equipment purchases
quarterly_data.figure: production 32 testers on capacity 60 (53% utilisation); raw materials KRW 71,340,885 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Market position and products: YC says it holds about 30% of the domestic memory wafer tester market, competing with Teradyne and Advantest, which hold over 80% of the global test equipment market. The NAND wafer tester MT6122 was co-developed with Samsung Electronics, the MT8311 (Polaris project) has shipped since H2 2024 and contributes to mass production, the MT6133 LPE-B extension is developed and in mass-production delivery, and a Polaris-H project and a next-generation tester (NGT) for the coming two to three years are under review; its earlier MT60xx and MT61xx testers remain reference tools in SK Hynix DRAM production. The company targets business expansion in Japan, the US, China and Taiwan. R&D spending was KRW 14,373 million (10.4% of revenue)
quarterly_data.figure: domestic memory wafer tester share about 30% (company); R&D KRW 14,373 million (10.4% of revenue)

quarterly_data.signal: Purchases: H1 2026 raw-material purchases of KRW 86,243 million, of which ICs were KRW 44,247 million (51.3%, main supplier Macus and others) and frames KRW 8,440 million (9.8%, from largest shareholder Samtec and others). Samsung Electronics holds 11.70% of YC's shares
quarterly_data.figure: ICs KRW 44,247 million (51.3% of purchases); frames KRW 8,440 million (9.8%)

connects_to.relationship: memory wafer testers (Samsung holds an 11.7% stake)
